question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate, and what deterministic allow, require-confirm, deny, and timeout rules should govern risky model-proposed tool calls?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing gate, but the permanent behavior changes the core authorization boundary, config contract, tool execution ordering, transcript semantics, and channel UX; automation cannot safely choose that policy.

options.title: Design The Core Gate
options.body: Approve a core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout handling, and tests around existing plugin approvals.

options.title: Keep Plugin-Only Approvals
options.body: Leave core execution unchanged and require operators or plugins to enforce contextual approval through before_tool_call.requireApproval and trusted tool policies.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Policy Work
options.body: Wait for related response-gate, action-level deny, MCP consent, and HITL interrupt designs to converge before adding a new config surface.

recommendation.title: Design The Core Gate
recommendation.body: Approve a core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout handling, and tests around existing plugin approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans security defaults, config compatibility, and the core agent execution loop; history and prior review route that product/security choice through this handle.
